Plan the coffee pack Specify whole beans or ground coffee, roast-to-pack timing and target shelf life. Confirm whether a degassing valve is needed and request its specification separately. Check fill volume with your actual coffee; a nominal gram size does not establish the right pouch dimensions. Plan the panels and filled base Review front, back, side panels and the flat base as separate artwork areas. Request the final dieline before placing copy across folds. Check the top opening and filled base dimensions against the filling and shelf requirements. Review the final heat seal Heat sealing is the recorded closing direction. Confirm seal width, film compatibility and the settings for the intended filling line. If repeat opening is required, specify a separate reopening or reclosing feature. Resolve the material references The material and film entries describe different levels of detail or alternative options. Choose one final layer structure in the quotation; do not combine the lists into an assumed laminate. Confirm layer order, thicknesses, sealant and the testing needed for the intended contents. Confirm size and measurement basis The fill-weight reference is 125g 250g 500g 1000g. Confirm usable internal dimensions and test the intended fill quantity with the actual contents; weight, volume and flat dimensions are not interchangeable. Approve the artwork and print route Share artwork status, the number of designs and quantity per design.
